answer: A payment bridge requires every agent to lock $100 for 30 days and allocates transaction capacity in proportion to locked funds. Fake identities can spread like a vine, but splitting $1,000 among ten agents buys no more capacity than bonding it to one. Viewed through this prism, identity count grants no extra power: an attacker seeking ten times the capacity must immobilize ten times the capital, paying its financing cost or forgoing its use elsewhere.
